data.description:

NORTH EAST, PA / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / NFI Empire, a fully owned subsidiary of Newport Gold, Inc. (OTCID:NWPG), today announced that Gannon University's MakerSpace has joined Project Reborn-001 as a technology and fabrication partner. The custom vehicle build is heading to auction at The Red Bird Games in Brentwood, TN, with proceeds benefiting The Brett Boyer Foundation. The MakerSpace is using advanced 3D-printing and design capabilities to create custom trim and badging components for this one-of-one Duramax dually.

The Build Update

Project Reborn-001 continues its transformation of a 1979 Chevrolet K30 crew cab into a modern performance powerhouse, pairing the classic square-body exterior with a contemporary GMC Sierra 3500 frame, Duramax diesel drivetrain, suspension, and amenities. Gannon University's MakerSpace is leveraging its advanced additive manufacturing capabilities to design and produce custom trim and badging pieces that either no longer exist or have never existed before. Through modern design tools and 3D-printing technology, the team is turning concepts into physical components that help complete the unique identity of Project REBORN. These contributions showcase what advanced manufacturing can accomplish on a one-of-one build while supporting the truck's path to SEMA and its live auction benefiting The Brett Boyer Foundation. Consistent progress updates will continue to be shared as the project advances.

"Project REBORN #001 is a great example of what can happen when creativity, technology and hands-on problem solving come together for a meaningful purpose. Through Gannon University's MakerSpace, we have the ability to take components that may no longer exist, or ideas that have never existed, and use modern design and 3D-printing technology to turn them into physical parts. Contributing custom trim and badging to this one-of-one build gives us an opportunity to showcase what advanced manufacturing can accomplish while supporting NFI Empire and, most importantly, the incredible work of The Brett Boyer Foundation. We're proud to have Gannon University's craftsmanship and innovation become part of the story of REBORN #001," said Nick Devine, Operations Manager, Gannon MakerSpace.

"Partnering with Gannon University's MakerSpace on Project Reborn-001 brings advanced manufacturing capability and local innovation that help solve challenges only a one-of-one build can present," said Justin Fried, CEO of Newport Gold, Inc. and NFI Empire. "Every component on this truck exists to amplify awareness and funding for The Brett Boyer Foundation's work against congenital heart disease and in celebration of the Down syndrome community."

What is The Brett Boyer Foundation

The Brett Boyer Foundation is a Nashville, Tennessee-based nonprofit charitable organization founded in 2017 by Ellen and Bo Boyer in loving memory of their daughter, Sadie Brett Boyer, who was diagnosed prenatally with Down syndrome and a congenital heart defect. Sadie Brett may have only lived for 7 months, but her impact has reached countless children and families, ultimately changing the medical industry by providing kids an edge and fighting chance against CHD. Congenital heart disease (CHD) is one of the most common conditions affecting infants and one that remains severely underfunded compared to other childhood illnesses. The Brett Boyer Foundation is dedicated to raising awareness and funding research aimed at advancing treatment options while providing support to families and providers navigating a CHD diagnosis. Another mission of The Brett Boyer Foundation is to celebrate the love, capability, and dignity of the Down syndrome community. 50% of babies born with Down syndrome fight CHD. Through fundraising efforts and partnerships with like-minded organizations both in the Nashville area and across the United States, the Foundation works to improve outcomes for children living with heart disease so that fewer families endure the loss the Boyers experienced.

The Brett Boyer Foundation: https://www.thebrettboyerfoundation.org/

About Gannon University MakerSpace

The Gannon University MakerSpace, located at the Center for Manufacturing and Technology in downtown Erie, Pennsylvania, is a hands-on innovation environment offering advanced capabilities in 3D printing (additive manufacturing), metal fabrication, woodworking, and electronics assembly. Designed to inspire creativity and collaboration, the MakerSpace serves students, small businesses, and community partners by providing access to cutting-edge tools and expertise that advance traditional manufacturing into a new age of technology. Learn more at https://makerspace.gannon.engineering/.

About NFI Empire

NFI Empire (NFIEmpire.com) is the wholly owned operating subsidiary of Newport Gold, Inc., a North East, Pennsylvania-based custom automotive company known for exclusive builds, high-performance vehicles, and deep technical and digital expertise across both traditional and digital automotive sectors. The Company has ceased all mining-related operations; Newport Gold is now a holding company whose operations are conducted entirely through NFI Empire. NFI Empire's stated goal is to become the first publicly traded automotive enthusiast company to integrate a brick-and-mortar business model with a proprietary technology platform.

data.title: BeOne Medicines Reports Sustained Survival Benefit with TEVIMBRA-ZIIHERA Combination in First-Line HER2+ Gastroesophageal Cancer | ONC Stock News
data.description:
The direct comparison with ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy did not reach statistical significance despite longer median survival with TEVIMBRA.

See more from StockTitan in Google Search and AI answers.Adds StockTitan as a preferred source · opens Google
Add on Google

New data from HERIZON-GEA-01 Phase 3 trial show 36-month overall survival of nearly 40% with TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy, and median OS reaching 27 months

TEVIMBRA-containing arm was associated with a four-month longer median OS compared with ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy

SAN CARLOS, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--BeOne Medicines Ltd. (Nasdaq: ONC; HKEX: 06160; SSE: 688235), a global oncology company, today announced new survival results from the planned second interim analysis (IA2) and final formal analysis of the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial, further confirming the benefit of TEVIMBRA® (tislelizumab) plus ZIIHERA® (zanidatamab) and chemotherapy as first-line treatment for patients with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA). The results will be presented today as a late-breaking abstract during a rapid oral session at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 in Madrid, Spain (LBA79).

Mark Lanasa, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer, Solid Tumors at BeOne, said:

“Following the U.S. approval in August, these longer-term data provide further evidence supporting TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy as the new standard of care in all first-line HER2-positive advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma patients, regardless of PD-L1 status. The magnitude of the survival benefit previously demonstrated with TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy increased after longer follow-up, with nearly 40% of patients receiving the TEVIMBRA-containing regimen alive at three years, representing a compelling result in this challenging disease area.”

Longer follow-up reinforces benefit of TEVIMBRA in combination regimen

This new analysis was conducted after 35.3 months of follow-up, an additional 9.4 months since the first interim analysis. Formal overall survival (OS) comparisons were tested sequentially, first comparing ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy and then comparing TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy with ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy.

Key findings include:

  • TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy demonstrated sustained long-term survival versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. Median OS was 27.0 months, with an OS hazard ratio (HR) of 0.65 (95% CI: 0.52-0.80), improved from 0.72 at the first interim analysis. This regimen is the only treatment for patients with HER2+ GEA to show a median overall survival of more than two years.
  • ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy significantly improved OS versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. Median OS was 22.9 months versus 19.6 months, respectively (HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.62-0.93; P=0.0088), meeting the remaining primary endpoint of the study.
  • Adding TEVIMBRA to ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy was associated with a four-month longer median OS at 27.0 months compared with ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy with 22.9 months (HR 0.81; 95% CI: 0.65-1.00). The difference did not reach statistical significance (P=0.0502) in the context of an underpowered analysis. A consistent trend toward improved OS was observed irrespective of PD-L1 status (PD-L1 TAP<1% HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.52-1.10; PD-L1 TAP≥1% HR 0.77; 95% CI: 0.58-1.02).
  • Long-term survival was highest with the TEVIMBRA-containing regimen. Estimated 36-month OS was 39.8% with TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy, 31.5% with ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy and 22.9% with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy.
  • TEVIMBRA plus ZIIHERA and chemotherapy significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy, with median PFS of 12.7 months versus 8.3 months (HR 0.61; 95% CI:0.5-0.76). Median PFS with ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy was 12.4 months versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy (HR 0.65; 95% CI:0.5-0.76).
  • The safety findings for both experimental arms were generally consistent with the first interim analysis, and with the known profiles of the component therapies. No new safety signals were identified, and diarrhea was the most common Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse event (TRAE). A mandatory anti-diarrheal prophylaxis was established during the first cycle, with most diarrhea events occurring early in the treatment.

About the HERIZON-GEA-01 Phase 3 Trial

HERIZON-GEA-01 (NCT05152147) is a global, randomized, open-label Phase 3 trial, conducted jointly with Jazz Pharmaceuticals, to evaluate and compare the efficacy and safety of ZIIHERA plus chemotherapy, with and without TEVIMBRA, to the standard of care (trastuzumab plus chemotherapy) as first-line treatment for adult patients with advanced/metastatic HER2+ GEA. The trial randomized 914 patients from approximately 300 trial sites in more than 30 countries. Patients for this trial had unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic HER2+ GEA (adenocarcinomas of the stomach or esophagus, including the gastroesophageal junction), defined as 3+ HER2 expression by IHC or 2+ HER2 expression by IHC with ISH positivity per central assessment. Patients were randomized to the three trial arms: ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy and TEVIMBRA; ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy; and trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. The trial evaluated dual primary endpoints, PFS per blinded independent central review (BICR) and OS.

About ZIIHERA (zanidatamab-hrii)

ZIIHERA (zanidatamab-hrii) is a bispecific human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, or HER2-directed antibody that binds to two extracellular sites on HER2. Binding of zanidatamab with HER2 results in internalization leading to a reduction in HER2 expression of the receptor on the tumor cell surface. Zanidatamab induces complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC), antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP). These mechanisms result in tumor growth inhibition and cell death in vitro and in vivo.1

Zanidatamab is being developed in multiple clinical trials as a targeted treatment option for patients with solid tumors that express HER2. Zanidatamab is approved in China for the treatment of patients who have unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic HER2-high expression (IHC 3+) biliary tract cancer (BTC) and who have received prior systemic therapy. ZIIHERA has also been granted accelerated approval in the U.S. and conditional marketing authorization in the European Union for eligible BTC patients. Zanidatamab is being developed by Jazz and BeOne under license agreements from Zymeworks, which first developed the molecule. BeOne has licensed zanidatamab from Zymeworks in Asia (excluding India and Japan), Australia and New Zealand. Jazz Pharmaceuticals has rights in all other regions.

ZIIHERA is a registered trademark of Zymeworks BC Inc.

About TEVIMBRA (tislelizumab)

TEVIMBRA is a uniquely designed humanized immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) monoclonal antibody with high affinity and binding specificity against PD-1. It is designed to minimize binding to Fc-gamma (Fcγ) receptors on macrophages, helping to aid the body’s immune cells to detect and fight tumors.

TEVIMBRA is the cornerstone asset of BeOne’s solid tumor portfolio and has shown potential across multiple tumor types and disease settings. The global TEVIMBRA clinical development program includes almost 15,000 patients enrolled to date in 30+ countries and regions across 71 trials, including 21 registration-enabling studies. TEVIMBRA is approved for various solid tumors (see prescribing information) in over 50 countries, and more than 2.2 million patients have been treated globally.

BeOne Medicines is a global oncology company that is discovering and developing innovative treatments for cancer patients worldwide. With a portfolio spanning hematology and solid tumors, BeOne is expediting development of its diverse pipeline of novel therapeutics through its internal capabilities and collaborations.   • Phase 3 RAINFOL™-02 trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) and its key secondary endpoint of overall survival (OS) with rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S®) compared to investigator’s choice chemotherapy
  • Results demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in PFS and OS in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC)
  • Data will be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting and discussed with regulatory authorities worldwide

COPENHAGEN, Denmark--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) announced today positive topline results from the global Phase 3 RAINFOL™-02 trial of rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S®), an investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeted, topoisomerase I (TOPO1)-inhibitor antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) regardless of FRα expression level or prior treatment with mirvetuximab. The trial met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS), with Rina-S demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement compared with investigator’s choice chemotherapy in the intent-to-treat (ITT) and in the primary analysis set (PAS) populations.

The ITT population (N=584) comprised of all randomized patients with PROC, regardless of FRα expression. The PAS population (N=492) mandated patients with FRα expression ≥75% PS2+ to have been treated with mirvetuximab.

In the ITT population, Rina-S demonstrated a 71% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death (HR 0.29; 95% CI, 0.23-0.37; p<0.0001). In the PAS population, Rina-S demonstrated a 67% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death (HR 0.33; 95% CI, 0.26–0.42; p<0.0001).

The study also met its key secondary endpoint of overall survival (OS), demonstrating a statically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in the ITT population (HR 0.43; 95% CI, 0.31–0.59; p<0.0001) and in the PAS population (HR 0.44; 95% CI, 0.31–0.63; p<0.0001).

The observed safety profile was consistent with the known profile of Rina-S, with no new safety signals or unexpected safety concerns identified.

“As the first Phase 3 readout from our Rina-S program, the positive topline results from RAINFOL-02 mark a significant milestone for Genmab and strengthen our confidence in Rina-S’s potential for patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. These results advance our ambition to become a leader in gynecologic oncology and reflect our commitment to improving the lives of patients with high unmet medical needs,” said Jan van de Winkel, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Genmab. “We look forward to discussing these results and potential next steps with regulatory authorities worldwide. We are deeply grateful to the patients, caregivers, and investigators whose participation made this study possible.”

Based on these results, Genmab plans to engage with regulatory authorities worldwide regarding potential next steps. The data will also be submitted for presentation at a future medical meeting.

“Platinum-resistant ovarian cancer remains one of the greatest challenges in gynecologic oncology, with patients often facing a poor prognosis and limited effective treatment options. The Phase 3 RAINFOL-02 results set a new benchmark in addressing this urgent unmet need regardless of FRα expression,” said Angeles Alvarez Secord, MD, MHSc, the study’s lead investigator for the Gynecologic Oncology Group (GOG) and Professor of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the Duke Cancer Institute. “The 71% reduction in the risk of disease progression and 57% reduction in the risk of death underscore the potential of Rina-S to change clinical practice if approved by offering a therapeutic option for a broad patient population.”

Rina-S is being evaluated in a broad clinical development program spanning multiple gynecologic cancers and other solid tumors. The program includes five Phase 3 trials evaluating Rina-S in PROC (RAINFOL-02; NCT06619236), recurrent or progressive endometrial cancer (RAINFOL-03; NCT07166094), platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC) maintenance therapy (RAINFOL-04; NCT07225270), second-line PSOC (RAINFOL-07; NCT07564141), and in first-line ovarian cancer as maintenance therapy (RAINFOL-10; NCT07859215). Additional studies include the Phase 1/2 RAINFOL-01 trial (NCT05579366) and Phase 2 trials in non-small cell lung cancer (RAINFOL-05; NCT07288177) and advanced gastrointestinal cancers (RAINFOL-09; NCT07539311).

On Wednesday, October 28 at 5:00 p.m. CET/12:00 p.m. EDT, Genmab will host an investor update. To register, visit genmab.com/events-presentations.

About the RAINFOL-02 Trial
RAINFOL-02 (NCT06619236) is a randomized, open-label, multicenter Phase 3 study evaluating the efficacy and safety of Rina-S versus investigator’s choice chemotherapy in 582 patients with PROC regardless of FRα expression level. Patients are randomized 1:1 to receive either Rina-S 120 mg/m² on Day 1 of each three-week treatment cycle or one of four standard-of-care chemotherapy agents: paclitaxel, topotecan, PLD, or gemcitabine. The primary endpoint is investigator-assessed PFS. Key secondary endpoints are OS and objective response rate (ORR). Other secondary endpoints include PFS by blinded independent central review, duration of response, incidence of adverse events and laboratory abnormalities, time from randomization to second disease progression or death, and change from baseline in global health status/quality of life. Efficacy is evaluated in two populations. The ITT population (N = 584) includes all randomized patients, regardless of FRα expression level. The PAS (N=492), a subset of the ITT population, includes only patients with FRα expression <75% PS2+ and patients previously treated with mirvetuximab if eligible based on FRα expression ≥75% PS2+ and available in the region.

About Ovarian Cancer
Ovarian cancer (OC) is a major global health issue, more than 320,000 new cases diagnosed annually worldwide.i It ranks as the eighth most common cancer and the eighth leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women globally.ii The disease is often diagnosed at an advanced stage because its symptoms, including abdominal bloating, pelvic pain and difficulty eating, can be subtle and nonspecific.iii Approximately 70-90% of women with advanced-stage OC worldwide experience a recurrence after initial treatment.iv OC has a low five-year survival rate, which varies significantly by region, but generally hovers around 30-50%.v,vi

Rina-S (GEN1184) is an investigational ADC. It is composed of a novel human monoclonal antibody directed at FRα, a hydrophilic protease-cleavable linker, and exatecan, a TOPO1 inhibitor payload. The clinical trial program for Rina-S continues to expand, including ovarian, endometrial, and other cancers with unmet need.

The safety and efficacy of Rina-S have not been established. Please visit https://clinicaltrials.gov/ for more information.

EMERYVILLE, Calif., Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kyverna Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: KYTX), a late-stage clinical immunology company pioneering transformative therapies for people with neurologic autoimmune diseases, today announced updated data from a Phase 1 investigator-initiated trial (IIT) of miv-cel (mivocabtagene autoleucel, KYV-101) in patients with progressive multiple sclerosis (PMS). The data will be shared today in an oral presentation at MS Toronto 2026, the joint ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS meeting.

“There remains a substantial unmet need for therapies that can meaningfully alter the course of progressive multiple sclerosis,” said Jeffrey Dunn, MD, Lily Sarafan Director of Neuroimmunology, Clinical Professor and Chief of Neuroimmunology at Stanford University. “In this early-phase study, miv-cel demonstrated encouraging tolerability, with evidence of CAR T-cell penetration into the central nervous system and biologic findings consistent with an immune reset. Importantly, we also observed sustained improvements in measures of neurologic disability and patient-reported function among evaluable participants. While these preliminary findings require confirmation in larger controlled trials, they provide an important proof of concept that miv-cel may offer a potential novel approach to treating progressive multiple sclerosis.”

Stanford Oral Presentation
Title: Safety and Preliminary Efficacy of CD-19 Directed CAR T-Cell Therapy in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A Phase 1 Study
Presenter: Jeff Dunn, M.D., Lily Sarafan Director of Neuroimmunology, Clinical Professor and Chief of Neuroimmunology, Stanford University
Date & Time: Friday, October 23, 2026, 11:05 – 11:15 AM ET

Stanford University is conducting an open-label, Phase 1, single-center study of miv-cel in patients with non-relapsing progressive multiple sclerosis, either secondary progressive MS (SPMS) or primary progressive MS (PPMS). Six patients were treated with either 33M (n=3) or 100M (n=3) CAR T-cell dose levels using a bendamustine lymphodepleting (LD) regimen.

The oral presentation features updated data from six patients with available efficacy data from five patients, with follow-up of more than two years in the longest-treated patient. Key highlights include:

Efficacy:

  • All five patients with available data demonstrated stable to improved expanded disability status scale scores (EDSS) as of last follow-up, with the majority (4/5) showing sustained clinical benefit through one year.
  • Four patients with more than one-year of follow-up sustained improvement without further need for chronic immunotherapies. The first patient treated with miv-cel achieved sustained clinical benefit beyond two years.

Biological activity:

  • Robust CAR T-cell expansion detected in peripheral blood and penetration in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), with peak levels at approximately day 14.
  • Complete depletion of CD19-positive peripheral B cells was achieved in all participants, followed by repopulation beginning at month 3, consistent with the emergence of naïve B cells, supporting evidence of immune reset.
  • Additional biomarker data, including CSF oligoclonal bands and kappa free light chain, continue to support favorable immunological impact at one year.

Safety:

  • Consistent, well-tolerated safety profile with no high-grade CRS and no reported cases of ICANS or IEC-HS.

“We are encouraged by the long-term durability and safety results with miv-cel in progressive multiple sclerosis, which add to the strong body of evidence supporting miv-cel’s transformative potential across neurologic autoimmune diseases,” said Naji Gehchan, Chief Medical and Development Officer of Kyverna Therapeutics. “The consistent, durable clinical benefit and well-tolerated safety profile observed across our indications are underpinned by miv-cel’s unique construct, specifically developed by Kyverna in autoimmune disease to enable immune reset by deeply and broadly depleting B-cells with a single dose. With our RMAT designation, we look forward to working with the FDA on our development plan in progressive multiple sclerosis and providing an update by early 2027.”

About miv-cel (mivocabtagene autoleucel, KYV-101)
Miv-cel is a fully human, autologous, CD19-targeting CAR T-cell therapy with CD28 co-stimulation. It is uniquely designed for potency and tolerability with the potential to achieve deep B-cell depletion, reset the immune system, and deliver durable drug-free, disease-free remission in autoimmune diseases with a single dose. Miv-cel is under investigation for B-cell driven autoimmune diseases and is produced using a well-established, validated manufacturing process. To date, more than 100 patients have been treated with miv-cel across a range of autoimmune diseases, and the clinical data demonstrates a consistent and well-tolerated safety profile.

About Multiple Sclerosis
Multiple sclerosis is a chronic autoimmune disease causing neurodegeneration, in which patients can experience a range of symptoms including blurred vision, slurred speech, tremors, numbness, extreme fatigue, problems with memory and concentration, and, in severe cases, the inability to walk or stand, B cells play a significant role in MS by producing autoantibodies that attack the protective sheath around the nerves, activating T cells, and increasing inflammation. Current disease-modifying treatments for MS aim to reduce the frequence of disease relapse and delay a progression of disability, but the disease remains a chronic condition that will progressively worsen for most patients.

About Kyverna Therapeutics
Kyverna Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: KYTX) is a late-stage clinical immunology company pioneering differentiated therapies with curative potential for neurologic autoimmune diseases. Kyverna’s lead autologous CD19-targeting CAR T-cell therapy candidate, miv-cel (mivocabtagene autoleucel, KYV-101), has demonstrated the potential to fundamentally change the treatment paradigm across multiple B-cell-driven autoimmune diseases. Kyverna is advancing its potentially first-in-class neuroimmunology franchise with its recently completed registrational trial in stiff person syndrome (SPS) and an ongoing registrational trial for generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG).

Miv-cel has received three FDA Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) designations, in SPS, gMG, and non-active secondary progressive multiple sclerosis (naSPMS) based on compelling clinical data and significant unmet need, further reinforcing the therapy's potential across neuroimmunology. Data reinforce the potential for immune reset with zolacabtagene autoleucel to address an underlying cause of multiple sclerosis

PRINCETON, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Bristol Myers Squibb (NYSE: BMY) today announced disclosure of interim safety and efficacy results from the multiple sclerosis (MS) cohorts of the Phase 1, single-arm, dose-escalation Breakfree-2 study evaluating zolacabtagene autoleucel (zola-cel; BMS-986353), an investigational, autologous CD19-directed CAR T cell therapy, in patients with highly active relapsing MS (haRMS) and progressive forms of MS (PMS). The data are being presented today in an oral presentation (Abstract #1615) at MSToronto 2026, the 10th Joint ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS Meeting taking place in Toronto, Canada.

The study included 66 patients (30 patients with haRMS and 36 patients with PMS) with ongoing disease activity or worsening disability despite treatment. Patients had a median of two prior disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) (range: 1-8 haRMS; 1-6 PMS). The primary endpoint of the study was safety, with efficacy as the secondary endpoint. The data presented show a safety profile consistent with previously reported zola-cel Phase 1 clinical trial data and early, promising efficacy across both haRMS and PMS with all patients treated at dose level 2 (DL2) (60/60) remaining off DMTs.

In the Breakfree-2 study, the majority of adverse events were brief and reversible, generally consistent with previously reported zola-cel Phase 1 clinical trial data.

  • Overall, 42.4% of patients (28/66) had cytokine release syndrome (CRS) events. Majority were Grade 1 (36.4%), with some Grade 2 (6.1%) and all resolved in a median of two days.
  • 7.6% of patients (5/66) had immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), most of which were Grade 1/2, which resolved in a median of two days.
  • One Grade 4 ICANS event occurred in a patient with PMS and was managed with corticosteroids and anakinra and resolved within four days.

After the data cutoff, one patient with haRMS experienced a fatal event of septic pneumonia. Following zola-cel infusion, the patient experienced late onset, non-ICANS motor symptoms that were not resolved by treatment with intermittent corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Although the patient’s CAR T cell expansion was consistent with that observed across the study, high-dose cyclophosphamide was administered and the patient developed septic pneumonia and died the following day, 44 days after infusion. No additional Grade 5 events have been reported across all zola-cel programs in autoimmune diseases, which include 190 patients treated in Phase 1 studies.

Secondary endpoints included measurements of efficacy, with zola-cel demonstrating potential for immune reset via complete B-cell depletion. At last follow up, all patients treated at DL2 (60/60) remained off DMTs, including nine patients with more than 12 months of follow-up.

Additional efficacy results from the study among evaluable patients (patients receiving DL2 with ≥ Week 26 follow-up; n=32) included:

  • Six of seven haRMS patients evaluable for no evidence of disease activity (NEDA) met criteria at ≥ Week 26, with all patients achieving no relapse, disability progression or MRI activity.
  • All eight haRMS patients evaluable for Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) at ≥ Week 26 demonstrated stability or improvement (range: 3.0-5.5 haRMS; 4.0-6.0 PMS).
  • Despite prior worsening at baseline, 22 of 24 (92%) PMS patients demonstrated stability or improvement in disability progression.
  • All 24 PMS patients demonstrated no new MRI activity.

“People living with relapsing and progressive forms of multiple sclerosis need treatment options that address the underlying disease while helping control relapses and preserve function,” said Dr. Jeffrey A. Cohen, Professor of Neurology and Staff Physician, Mellen Center, Cleveland Clinic. “These data suggest that CD19-directed CAR T cell therapy may offer a new approach to treating multiple sclerosis. While more research is needed, the potential to control relapses, stabilize disability and reduce reliance on disease-modifying medications is encouraging.”

“BMS is at the forefront of cell therapy science, pioneering a new era by exploring the potential for immune reset in patients living with autoimmune diseases,” said Lynelle B. Hoch, president, Cell Therapy Organization, Bristol Myers Squibb. “The Breakfree-2 data demonstrate clinical potential for zola-cel in multiple sclerosis, showcasing the opportunity for treatment-free remission in patients who have depended on chronic therapies for years. We are advancing zola-cel with the goal to redefine autoimmune care with a single, transformative treatment.”

Bristol Myers Squibb extends its gratitude to the patients, families and investigators involved in the Breakfree-2 clinical trial.

About the Breakfree-2 Study

Breakfree-2 (NCT06220201) is a Phase 1, multicenter, single-arm, dose-escalation study evaluating the safety and efficacy of zolacabtagene autoleucel (zola-cel; BMS-986353), in patients with autoimmune neurological diseases: relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, progressive forms of multiple sclerosis or refractory myasthenia gravis. Zola-cel is an investigational CD19-directed CAR T cell therapy that expresses the CD19 CAR and is manufactured using a next-generation process (NEX-T™). This platform uses an intentional five-day manufacturing process optimized so the CAR T cells reach a stable vector integration and early-differentiated phenotype prior to infusion.

Trial patients across cohorts follow a similar process: apheresis to collect T cells, after which the cells are manufactured into CD19 CAR T cells at specialized facilities utilizing the NEX-T manufacturing process. After undergoing lymphodepletion, patients receive a single infusion of zola-cel.

The primary endpoint is safety. Key secondary endpoints include number of patients meeting no evidence of disease activity criteria, number of patients with confirmed disability progression confirmed per EDSS, as well as pharmacokinetic outcomes.

A pioneer in harnessing the immune system to fight cancer and an established leader in cell therapy, Bristol Myers Squibb is uniquely positioned to unlock the full potential of this technology across blood cancers and within new frontiers, including autoimmune disease.

Bristol Myers Squibb is currently the only company with two approved CAR T cell therapies with two distinct targets, available in major markets around the world. Our bold vision for the future is one in which hundreds of thousands of patients can be treated with cell therapy’s transformational potential.

The building blocks to realize this ambition – a promising and differentiated pipeline, extensive translational and clinical data sets, a deep bench of talent, and robust manufacturing capabilities – are in our cells. We are laser-focused on advancing the field of cell therapy toward a true revolution for patients. Learn more about the science behind cell therapy and ongoing progress at Bristol Myers Squibb here.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Perfect Corp. (NYSE: PERF), a global leader in augmented reality (AR) and artificial intelligence (AI) beauty and fashion tech, today announced that YouCam is one of the first platforms to integrate the newly released Kling 4.0 API. The newest AI video model from Kuaishou Technology’s Kling AI is now live across the YouCam lineup on mobile and web. Built for longer storytelling, Kling 4.0 lets users set up to 10 keyframes instead of only a first and last frame, then generates up to 30 seconds of continuous video with lip-synced dialogue and stereo sound in a single pass.

YouCam Integrates Newly Released Kling 4.0 API to Turn Photos into 30-Second Stories with Dialogue and Sound

Kling 4.0 in YouCam at a Glance

  • Up to 10 keyframes: set the key moments of a story, like a storyboard
  • 30 seconds in one generation: twice the length of Kling 3.0, as one continuous take
  • Sound built in: dialogue, sound effects, and stereo audio come with the video
  • Multilingual speech: 9+ languages and several English accents, with matching lip movement
  • Mixed references: photos, character sheets, and video clips keep faces and products consistent
  • Trend remakes: reuse the pacing and shots of a reference video with new products and people

Plan the Story Before Generating the Video with Up to 10 Keyframes

Keyframes let users define what should appear at selected points in a video. Rather than describing an entire sequence in one prompt, users can establish its opening, intermediate moments, and ending, then provide instructions for movement and camera direction.

Kling 4.0 supports up to 10 keyframes and up to 30 seconds per generation in YouCam. These controls let users structure a short film scene, a product launch video, or a character-led story before generating it.

For example, an AI filmmaker can storyboard a 30-second scene in which a traveler steps off a night train, crosses a crowded platform, spots a stranger holding her lost suitcase, and stops face to face with him as the train pulls away. The keyframes fix each story beat in place, while the prompt describes the action, camera movement, and dialogue that connect them.

“The hardest part of AI video has been getting the model to follow your plan instead of guessing,” said Alice Chang, Founder & CEO of Perfect Corp. “Kling 4.0 lets YouCam users set up to 10 moments in a story and decide what each character says, so the video ends up the way they imagined it.”

Keep the Same Faces and Products in Every Shot

A longer story only works if its people and objects stay the same from scene to scene. Kling 4.0 accepts many kinds of references in one task, including photos, character sheets that show a person from several angles, storyboards, and short video clips that show how someone moves or how the camera should travel. The model uses them together to keep faces, outfits, and product details consistent throughout the video.

A consumer electronics brand can upload photos of its new wireless earbuds, a character sheet for its on-screen host, and a short clip showing the camera move it wants, then generate a launch video in which the earbuds and the host look the same in every scene.

Develop Dialogue Alongside the Visual Story

Every Kling 4.0 video can come with its own soundtrack. The model generates dialogue, background sound, and sound effects together with the picture, outputs them in two-channel stereo, and matches mouth movement to speech more closely than earlier Kling models.

Trend Remakes with a Reference Video

Users can also start from a video they like. With reference videos, such as a popular unboxing format, a travel vlog, or one of their own best-performing posts, Kling 4.0 follows its pacing, shot order, and presentation style, then replaces the products and people with the user’s own.

A brand can take one proven format and turn it into a separate video for every product in its lineup, and a video creator can join a trend with their own characters and story without planning every shot again.

First reported clinical evaluation of an allogeneic CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in progressive MS demonstrated an encouraging preliminary safety profile with no high-grade CAR-T associated toxicities observed

89% of evaluable participants (16/19) had stable or improved disability scores at Day 90, despite documented progression prior to enrollment on high-efficacy therapies

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--TG Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: TGTX), today announced initial results from the Company’s Phase 1 study evaluating azercabtagene zapreleucel (azer-cel), an investigational, allogeneic CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, in patients with progressive multiple sclerosis (MS). The data represent the first reported clinical evaluation of an allogeneic CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in progressive MS and were presented in a late-breaking oral session at MSToronto2026, the 10th Joint Meeting of the Americas and European Committees for Treatment and Research in Multiple Sclerosis (ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS), being held October 21–23, 2026, in Toronto, Canada.

Michael S. Weiss, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of TG Therapeutics, stated, “These initial azer-cel results are particularly encouraging given that all patients entered the study with progressive disability despite prior treatment with high-efficacy therapies, including anti-CD20 treatment. The safety findings to date, together with evidence of B-cell depletion in both the blood and cerebrospinal fluid, demonstrate biological activity at doses that appear tolerable, while stable or improved disability scores in most subjects provide a potential signal of clinical activity. Of particular interest, five of the 18 evaluable patients experienced improvements in disability scores, including three patients with improvements of two or more points on the EDSS scale, an encouraging early finding in a disease where even slowing progression can represent an important therapeutic advance.”

Mr. Weiss continued, “While these results remain preliminary, we believe an off-the-shelf CAR T-cell therapy has the potential to offer a meaningful new treatment option for patients with progressive MS, where substantial unmet need remains. We look forward to continuing dose escalation and evaluating longer-term outcomes, and we are grateful to the patients, their families, and the clinical teams who are making this research possible.”

TG PRESENTATION:

Late-Breaking Oral Presentation: First Clinical Evaluation of an Allogeneic CD19-Directed CAR T-Cell Therapy in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: Initial Results from the Phase 1 TG-Azercel-101 Study

The presentation includes data from 26 participants with progressive MS treated across six azer-cel dose levels, ranging from 30 million to 500 million CAR T-cells, following bendamustine lymphodepletion. All participants had experienced progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) within the prior 12 months despite high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy, and all had previously received anti-CD20 therapy. The median baseline EDSS score was 6.0, reflecting substantial disability, with patients typically requiring assistance to walk even relatively short distances. As of the September 3, 2026 data cutoff, median follow-up was 4.9 months, with a range of 0.1 to 15.0 months.

Presentation Highlights:

  • Azer-cel demonstrated an encouraging initial safety profile in 26 participants, with no dose-limiting toxicities or high-grade CAR T associated toxicities observed across dose levels including no Grade ≥3 cytokine release syndrome (CRS), Grade ≥2 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), graft-versus-host disease, immune effector cell-associated hemophagocytic syndrome (IEC-HS) and no Grade ≥3 infections.
  • Despite documented progression prior to enrollment, EDSS scores were stable or improved in 89% of evaluable participants at Day 90 (16/18) and 88% at Day 180 (7/8). Three participants achieved EDSS improvements of at least 2.0 points at Day 90, including one with a 4.0-point improvement.
  • At Day 90, most evaluable participants demonstrated stable or improved walking performance (94%; 16/17), upper extremity function (94%; 17/18) and cognitive processing speed (78%; 14/18), with no gadolinium-enhancing T1 lesions or new or enlarging T2 lesions observed in any of the 22 participants evaluable by MRI.
  • Peripheral blood B-cell counts were depleted to below 10 cells/µL in 96% of participants (25/26), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples from 21 participants showed a median reduction in CD19-positive B-cell events of 52.3% at Day 10. B-cell reconstitution was observed as early as Day 42 and favored transitional and naïve populations.

These initial findings are from an ongoing, open-label Phase 1 study and are limited by the small number of participants and short follow-up. Dose escalation and longer-term follow-up are ongoing.

The full data presentation is also available on the Publications page of the Company’s website at https://www.tgtherapeutics.com/publications/.

ABOUT BRIUMVI® (ublituximab-xiiy) 150 mg/6 mL Injection for IV
BRIUMVI is a novel monoclonal antibody that targets a unique epitope on CD20-expressing B-cells. Targeting CD20 using monoclonal antibodies has proven to be an important therapeutic approach for the management of autoimmune disorders, such as RMS. BRIUMVI is uniquely designed to lack certain sugar molecules normally expressed on the antibody. Removal of these sugar molecules, a process called glycoengineering, allows for efficient B-cell depletion at low doses.

BRIUMVI is indicated in the U.S. for the treatment of adults with RMS, including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease and in several countries outside of the U.S. for the treatment of adult patients with RMS with active disease defined by clinical or imaging features.

A list of authorized specialty distributors can be found at www.briumvi.com.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION
Contraindications: BRIUMVI is contraindicated in patients with:

  • Active Hepatitis B Virus infection
  • A history of life-threatening infusion reaction to BRIUMVI

WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS

Infusion Reactions: BRIUMVI can cause infusion reactions, which can include pyrexia, chills, headache, influenza-like illness, tachycardia, nausea, throat irritation, erythema, and an anaphylactic reaction. In MS clinical trials, the incidence of infusion reactions in BRIUMVI-treated patients who received infusion reaction-limiting premedication prior to each infusion was 48%, with the highest incidence within 24 hours of the first infusion. 0.6% of BRIUMVI-treated patients experienced infusion reactions that were serious, some requiring hospitalization.

Observe treated patients for infusion reactions during the infusion and for at least one hour after the completion of the first two infusions unless infusion reaction and/or hypersensitivity has been observed in association with the current or any prior infusion. Inform patients that infusion reactions can occur up to 24 hours after the infusion. Administer the recommended pre-medication to reduce the frequency and severity of infusion reactions. If life-threatening, stop the infusion immediately, permanently discontinue BRIUMVI, and administer appropriate supportive treatment. Less severe infusion reactions may involve temporarily stopping the infusion, reducing the infusion rate, and/or administering symptomatic treatment.

Infections: Serious, life-threatening or fatal, bacterial and viral infections have been reported in BRIUMVI-treated patients. In MS clinical trials, the overall rate of infections in BRIUMVI-treated patients was 56% compared to 54% in teriflunomide-treated patients. The rate of serious infections was 5% compared to 3% respectively. There were 3 infection-related deaths in BRIUMVI-treated patients. The most common infections in BRIUMVI-treated patients included upper respiratory tract infection (45%) and urinary tract infection (10%). Delay BRIUMVI administration in patients with an active infection until the infection is resolved.

Consider the potential for increased immunosuppressive effects when initiating BRIUMVI after immunosuppressive therapy or initiating an immunosuppressive therapy after BRIUMVI.

Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Reactivation: HBV reactivation occurred in an MS patient treated with BRIUMVI in clinical trials. Fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, and death caused by HBV reactivation have occurred in patients treated with anti-CD20 antibodies. Perform HBV screening in all patients before initiation of treatment with BRIUMVI. Do not start treatment with BRIUMVI in patients with active HBV confirmed by positive results for HB surface antigen (HBsAg) and anti-HB tests. For patients who are negative for HBsAg and positive for HB core antibody [HBcAb+] or are carriers of HBV [HBsAg+], consult a liver disease expert before starting and during treatment.

Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML): PML is an opportunistic viral infection of the brain caused by the JC virus (JCV) that typically only occurs in patients who are immunocompromised, and that usually leads to death or severe disability. JCV infection resulting in PML has been observed in patients treated with anti-CD20 antibodies, including BRIUMVI, and other MS therapies.

If PML is suspected, withhold BRIUMVI and perform an appropriate diagnostic evaluation. Typical symptoms associated with PML are diverse, progress over days to weeks, and include progressive weakness on one side of the body or clumsiness of limbs, disturbance of vision, and changes in thinking, memory, and orientation leading to confusion and personality changes.

MRI findings may be apparent before clinical signs or symptoms; monitoring for signs consistent with PML may be useful. Further investigate suspicious findings to allow for an early diagnosis of PML, if present. Following discontinuation of another MS medication associated with PML, lower PML-related mortality and morbidity have been reported in patients who were initially asymptomatic at diagnosis compared to patients who had characteristic clinical signs and symptoms at diagnosis.

If PML is confirmed, treatment with BRIUMVI should be discontinued.

Vaccinations: Administer all immunizations according to immunization guidelines: for live or live-attenuated vaccines, at least 4 weeks and, whenever possible, at least 2 weeks prior to initiation of BRIUMVI for non-live vaccines. BRIUMVI may interfere with the effectiveness of non-live vaccines. The safety of immunization with live or live-attenuated vaccines during or following administration of BRIUMVI has not been studied. Vaccination with live virus vaccines is not recommended during treatment and until B-cell repletion.

Vaccination of Infants Born to Mothers Treated with BRIUMVI During Pregnancy: In infants of mothers exposed to BRIUMVI during pregnancy, assess B-cell counts prior to administration of live or live-attenuated vaccines as measured by CD19+ B-cells. Depletion of B-cells in these infants may increase the risks from live or live-attenuated vaccines. Inactivated or non-live vaccines may be administered prior to B-cell recovery. Assessment of vaccine immune responses, including consultation with a qualified specialist, should be considered to determine whether a protective immune response was mounted.

Fetal Risk: Based on data from animal studies, BRIUMVI may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Transient peripheral B-cell depletion and lymphocytopenia have been reported in infants born to mothers exposed to other anti-CD20 B-cell depleting antibodies during pregnancy. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during BRIUMVI treatment and for 6 months after the last dose.

Reduction in Immunoglobulins: As expected with any B-cell depleting therapy, decreased immunoglobulin levels were observed. Decrease in immunoglobulin M (IgM) was reported in 0.6% of BRIUMVI-treated patients compared to none of the patients treated with teriflunomide in RMS clinical trials. Monitor the levels of quantitative serum immunoglobulins during treatment, especially in patients with opportunistic or recurrent infections, and after discontinuation of therapy, until B-cell repletion. Consider discontinuing BRIUMVI therapy if a patient with low immunoglobulins develops a serious opportunistic infection or recurrent infections, or if prolonged hypogammaglobulinemia requires treatment with intravenous immunoglobulins.

Liver Injury: Clinically significant liver injury, without findings of viral hepatitis, has been reported in the postmarketing setting in patients treated with anti-CD20 B-cell depleting therapies approved for the treatment of MS, including BRIUMVI. Signs of liver injury, including markedly elevated serum hepatic enzymes with elevated total bilirubin, have occurred from weeks to months after administration.

Patients treated with BRIUMVI found to have an alanine aminotransaminase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) greater than 3x the upper limit of normal (ULN) with serum total bilirubin greater than 2x ULN are potentially at risk for severe drug-induced liver injury.

Obtain liver function tests prior to initiating treatment with BRIUMVI, and monitor for signs and symptoms of any hepatic injury during treatment. Measure serum aminotransferases, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin levels promptly in patients who report symptoms that may indicate liver injury, including new or worsening fatigue, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, right upper abdominal discomfort, dark urine, or jaundice. If liver injury is present and an alternative etiology is not identified, discontinue BRIUMVI.

Most Common Adverse Reactions: The most common adverse reactions in RMS trials (incidence of at least 10%) were infusion reactions and upper respiratory tract infections.

Physicians, pharmacists, or other healthcare professionals with questions about BRIUMVI should visit www.briumvi.com.

Key Terms

progression independent of relapse activitymedical
Progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) is a measure used in multiple sclerosis clinical research to describe a sustained increase in neurological disability that occurs without an intervening clinical relapse. It is identified when a patient shows confirmed worsening on a standardized disability scale (for example, a lasting increase in Expanded Disability Status Scale score or another pre-specified clinical test) that is not preceded or accompanied by a relapse within the trial’s defined time window, so the worsening is attributed to underlying, non-relapse disease activity rather than an acute attack. How PIRA is counted depends on the study’s specific definitions of ‘‘relapse’’ and the required confirmation period, so comparisons across studies require attention to those criteria.
edssmedical
EDSS (Expanded Disability Status Scale) is a clinical scale used to quantify disability in people with multiple sclerosis. It runs from 0 (normal neurological exam) to 10 (death from MS) in 0.5-point steps and is based chiefly on neurological examination findings and walking ability; higher scores indicate greater disability. The scale is more sensitive to changes in mobility and ambulation than to cognitive, visual, or fatigue-related impairments, so small score changes do not reflect all kinds of clinical change equally.
cytokine release syndromemedical
An intense immune overreaction in which the body's defense system releases a large surge of signaling proteins, causing fever, low blood pressure, breathing trouble or organ stress; imagine the immune system's alarm going into overdrive and flooding the body with emergency responders. Investors care because this side effect can slow or block regulatory approval, increase clinical trial costs and liabilities, limit how widely a therapy can be used, and therefore affect a drug's market value and sales potential.
immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndromemedical
immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) is a brain-related side effect that can occur after treatments that activate powerful immune cells, such as engineered cell therapies. It can cause confusion, speech problems, seizures or coma when the immune response unintentionally harms brain function; think of an overenthusiastic security system that starts damaging the house it’s protecting. Investors care because ICANS affects clinical trial results, regulatory approvals, product labeling, treatment adoption, monitoring costs and potential liability, all of which influence a therapy’s commercial value.
graft-versus-host diseasemedical
Graft-versus-host disease is a complication that can occur after a transplant using donor immune cells, where those transplanted cells attack the recipient’s organs and skin instead of protecting them; imagine a new security team mistaking the building’s occupants for intruders. It matters to investors because its likelihood, severity, and available treatments shape clinical trial results, drug approval chances, safety labels, patient outcomes, and the commercial potential of therapies aimed at preventing or managing the condition.
lymphodepletionmedical
Lymphodepletion is a short medical treatment that lowers a patient’s lymphocytes, the immune cells that can interfere with certain cell-based therapies, to create a more supportive environment for the new therapy to work. Think of it like clearing a crowded garden bed before planting seeds: by temporarily reducing competing cells, the engineered therapy can take hold more effectively. Investors watch lymphodepletion because it affects clinical trial results, safety profiles, treatment adoption, and overall commercial potential.

Western Alliance 100 was designed around a simple idea: Leaders make stronger decisions when they have access to informed perspectives, candid conversation and people who understand the opportunities and challenges their businesses face. Across two days of presentations, moderated conversations, panel discussions and peer connections, Western Alliance 100 explored leadership, market volatility, artificial intelligence, demographic change, economic and policy conditions, cybersecurity, housing and Arizona’s continued development. The program also included four breakout sessions focused on emerging technologies, economic conditions, the housing market and Arizona’s growth.

Our goal was not to tell clients what to think, but to create the kind of candid exchange that helps leaders challenge assumptions, consider different points of view and determine the right path for their businesses.”

Western Alliance 100 featured leaders and experts from business, government, sports and other fields. President George W. Bush joined the forum for a wide-ranging conversation about his time in the White House, the challenges facing the nation and lessons learned throughout his career. The discussion covered pivotal moments of his presidency, navigating difficult decisions, the evolving global landscape and the importance of leadership, service and finding common ground.

The broader program paired high-level perspectives with practical discussion. Featured speakers included former Duke University men’s basketball coach Mike Krzyzewski, known as Coach K, on team building and resilience; Fundstrat Capital’s Tom Lee on market performance and volatility; AI executive and author Sol Rashidi on bringing artificial intelligence to market; and MIT AgeLab founder Dr. Joseph Coughlin on the business implications of demographic change. Breakout discussions explored AI, cybersecurity and emerging technologies, economic conditions, mortgage rates and housing policy plus the projects reshaping Arizona’s future. A bipartisan panel featuring Karl Rove and Paul Begala shared unique perspectives from their decades of election experience ahead of the midterm elections.

“Our clients expect more than access to financial products. They need people who understand their businesses, know their industries and can bring the right expertise to the table when an important decision arises,” Vecchione said. “We appreciate our role as trusted business advisors to our clients in more than 30 different industries, all across the country.”

The forum reflected Western Alliance’s relationship banking model, Arizona roots and expanding national perspective. The bank connects direct client relationships with specialized expertise, tailored solutions and national capabilities to help businesses make clearer decisions, respond to change and act on opportunity. The event also created opportunities for clients to connect with peers, share ideas and build relationships that may support future growth.

“Bringing leaders from around the country together in Arizona created an opportunity to hear perspectives from outside their normal circles, test ideas and build business relationships that can support growth well beyond the event,” Vecchione said. “That is what we want Western Alliance 100 to represent.”

Add on Google

Nearly 40% of patients alive at three years with Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy, irrespective of PD-L1 status, achieving a median OS of 27 months

Mature HERIZON-GEA-01 results show Ziihera plus chemotherapy delivered statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS benefit, reducing the risk of death by 24% versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy

For U.S. media and investors only

DUBLIN, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc (Nasdaq: JAZZ) today announced updated overall survival (OS) results from the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial evaluating Ziihera® (zanidatamab-hrii) in combination with chemotherapy, with or without Tevimbra® (tislelizumab-jsgr), as first-line treatment for adults with HER2-positive (HER2+) locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA). The results from the second interim, and final formal, analysis were presented as a late-breaking rapid oral presentation (LBA79) at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 in Madrid, Spain.

"For patients with HER2+ advanced GEA, long-term survival remains difficult to achieve. With longer follow-up, Ziihera-containing regimens demonstrated a durable overall survival benefit, with nearly 40% of patients treated with Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy alive at three years," said Dr. Kohei Shitara, director of the Department of Gastrointestinal Oncology, and principal trial investigator at the National Cancer Center Hospital East, Kashiwa, Japan. "Ziihera plus chemotherapy has also now demonstrated a statistically significant survival benefit over trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. Together, these findings provide strong evidence for Ziihera-containing regimens as the new HER2-directed first-line standard of care."

At the data cutoff, median follow-up was 35.3 months, 9.4 months longer than at the first interim analysis. Key findings included:

  • Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy sustained its OS benefit versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy, with an improved HR: Median OS reached 27.0 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 23.7-32.2), the longest reported in a Phase 3 trial in this setting, compared with 19.6 months with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. The Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy regimen reduced the risk of death by 35% (hazard ratio [HR] 0.65; 95% CI: 0.52-0.80), improving from an HR of 0.72 at the first interim analysis.
  • Nearly 40% of patients receiving Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy were alive at three years: Estimated 36-month OS was 39.8% with Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy, 31.5% with Ziihera plus chemotherapy and 22.9% with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy.
  • Ziihera plus chemotherapy demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful OS improvement versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy: Median OS was 22.9 months (95% CI: 19.9-27.6) with Ziihera plus chemotherapy compared with 19.6 months (95% CI: 16.9-22.2) with trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. Ziihera plus chemotherapy reduced the risk of death by 24% (HR 0.76; 95% CI: 0.62-0.93; P=0.0088).
  • Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy showed a meaningful trend toward improved OS versus Ziihera plus chemotherapy: Median OS was approximately four months longer with Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy than with Ziihera plus chemotherapy (27.0 versus 22.9 months; HR 0.81; 95% CI: 0.65-1.00; P=0.0502). The difference did not reach statistical significance. Mean duration of treatment was longest for Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy (64.1 weeks): 11.5 weeks longer than Ziihera plus chemotherapy (52.6 weeks), and 21.8 weeks longer than trastuzumab plus chemotherapy (42.3 weeks).
  • Safety profiles remained unchanged with longer follow-up: The safety profiles of both Ziihera-containing regimens were consistent with the first interim analysis, supporting the tolerability of prolonged treatment.

"These HERIZON-GEA-01 three-year landmark results demonstrate meaningful survival outcomes for patients with HER2+ advanced GEA," said Rob Iannone, M.D., M.S.C.E., executive vice president, global head of R&D, and chief medical officer of Jazz Pharmaceuticals. "The statistically significant survival benefit observed with Ziihera plus chemotherapy and the durable outcomes seen with Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy cement Ziihera as the new HER2-targeted backbone therapy in first-line HER2+ advanced GEA."

The Ziihera-containing regimens were recently included as preferred therapies in the National Comprehensive Cancer Network® (NCCN®) Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology® for Gastric Cancer, and Esophageal and Esophagogastric Junction Cancers, and Ziihera plus tislelizumab and chemotherapy is the only preferred HER2+ regimen irrespective of PD-L1 status.

These results follow the August 25, 2026, U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of two Ziihera-containing regimens for the first-line treatment of adults with HER2+ unresectable locally advanced or metastatic GEA: Ziihera plus tislelizumab and fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy for adults with HER2+ IHC 3+ or IHC 2+/ISH+ disease; and Ziihera plus fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy for adults with HER2+ IHC 3+ disease. The approval was based on results from the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 trial, which were first presented at ASCO GI 2026, subsequently published in The New England Journal of Medicine and further evaluated through PD-L1 subgroup analyses presented at ASCO 2026.

The U.S. Prescribing Information for Ziihera contains Boxed Warnings for diarrhea and embryo-fetal toxicity.

Additional Important Safety Information related to Ziihera use in GEA is provided below. Please see full Prescription, including Boxed Warnings at https://pp.jazzpharma.com/pi/ziihera.en.USPI.pdf.

About the Phase 3 HERIZON-GEA-01 Trial
HERIZON-GEA-01 (NCT05152147) is a global, randomized, open-label Phase 3 trial, conducted jointly with BeOne Medicines, to evaluate and compare the efficacy and safety of zanidatamab plus chemotherapy, with and without tislelizumab, to trastuzumab plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment for adult patients with advanced/metastatic HER2+ GEA. The trial randomized 914 patients from approximately 225 trial sites in more than 30 countries. Appropriate patients for this trial had unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic HER2+ GEA (adenocarcinomas of the stomach or esophagus, including the gastroesophageal junction), defined as 3+ HER2 expression by IHC or 2+ HER2 expression by IHC with ISH positivity per central assessment. Patients were randomized to the three trial arms: zanidatamab in combination with chemotherapy and tislelizumab; zanidatamab in combination with chemotherapy; and trastuzumab plus chemotherapy. The trial evaluated dual primary endpoints, PFS per blinded independent central review (BICR) and OS.

About Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma
GEA, including cancers of the stomach, gastroesophageal junction, and esophagus, is the fifth most common cancer worldwide, and approximately 20% of patients have HER2+ disease.1,2,3,4 HER2+ GEA has high morbidity and mortality, and patients are urgently in need of new treatment options. The overall prognosis for patients with GEA remains poor, with a global five-year survival rate of less than 10% for metastatic disease.5

About Ziihera® (zanidatamab-hrii)
Ziihera (zanidatamab-hrii) is a bispecific HER2-directed antibody that binds to two extracellular sites on HER2. Binding of zanidatamab with HER2 results in internalization leading to a reduction in HER2 expression of the receptor on the tumor cell surface. Zanidatamab induces CDC, ADCC, and ADCP. These mechanisms result in tumor growth inhibition and cell death in vitro and in vivo.6

Gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA): In the United States, Ziihera is indicated for the first-line treatment of adults with HER2+ locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA), including cancers of the stomach, gastroesophageal junction and esophagus, in combination with tislelizumab-jsgr and fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy (HER2+ IHC 3+ and IHC 2+/ISH+ as detected by an FDA-authorized test); and in combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy (HER2+ IHC 3+ as detected by an FDA-authorized test).

Biliary tract cancer (BTC): In the United States, Ziihera is also indicated for the treatment of adults with previously treated, unresectable or metastatic HER2+ (IHC 3+) biliary tract cancer (BTC), as detected by an FDA-approved test.6 Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).6 Ziihera is also approved in the European Union and other countries.

Zanidatamab is being developed in multiple clinical trials as a targeted treatment option for patients with solid tumors that express HER2. Zanidatamab is being developed by Jazz and BeOne Medicines under license agreements from Zymeworks, which first developed the molecule.

The FDA granted three Breakthrough Therapy designations for zanidatamab's development: one as a single agent for previously treated HER2 gene-amplified BTC, one in combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy, with or without tislelizumab for first-line HER2+ unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastric, gastroesophageal junction (GEJ), or esophageal GEA, and one for the treatment of adults with previously treated, locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic HER2+ colorectal cancer (CRC). The FDA also granted two Fast Track designations for zanidatamab: one as a single agent for refractory BTC and one in combination with standard-of-care chemotherapy for first-line GEA. Additionally, zanidatamab has received Orphan Drug designations from the FDA for the treatment of BTC, gastric (including GEJ) cancer, and esophageal cancer, as well as Orphan Drug designations from the European Medicines Agency for the treatment of BTC, gastric/gastroesophageal junction cancer, and esophageal cancer. Jazz continues to pursue additional regulatory approvals for zanidatamab in markets worldwide.

Important Safety Information for ZIIHERA 

WARNING: DIARRHEA and EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY

 

ZIIHERA, in combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy, with or without
tislelizumab-jsgr, can cause severe diarrhea, including life threatening and fatal cases. Use antidiarrheal
prophylaxis during the first cycle when ZIIHERA is given in combination with these drugs. Manage with
antidiarrheals and supportive measures as clinically indicated. Interrupt, reduce the dose or discontinue
ZIIHERA based on severity. 

 

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: Exposure to ZIIHERA during pregnancy can cause embryo-fetal harm. Advise patients
of the risk and need for effective contraception.

Diarrhea: ZIIHERA can cause severe diarrhea.

When ZIIHERA is used in combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy with or without tislelizumab-jsgr, severe, life threatening, and fatal cases of diarrhea can occur despite loperamide prophylaxis. The risk of severe and life threatening diarrhea is higher when ZIIHERA is administered with chemotherapy and tislelizumab-jsgr, with a higher risk in patients aged ≥ 65 years compared to younger patients. Advise patients to increase oral fluids, begin antidiarrheals, and notify their healthcare provider immediately if diarrhea occurs.

Administer antidiarrheal prophylaxis with loperamide in cycle 1 for all patients receiving ZIIHERA in combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-containing chemotherapy with or without tislelizumab-jsgr. Begin loperamide at the first loose stool when ZIIHERA is administered in combination with chemotherapy. Administer fluids, electrolytes, and additional antidiarrheal agents as necessary. Before modifying the dose of ZIIHERA, evaluate, modify or discontinue drug(s) contributing to diarrhea in accordance with their respective prescribing information. Withhold, reduce the dose, or permanently discontinue ZIIHERA based on severity.

If treating patients with ZIIHERA in combination with FOLFOX, do not administer the fluorouracil bolus.

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy and tislelizumab-jsgr

Diarrhea was reported in 85% of 330 patients in clinical studies, including Grade 4 (2.1%), Grade 3 (24%), and Grade 2 (31%) events. Fatal outcomes resulting from diarrhea occurred in 1.5% of patients. Diarrhea leading to dose reduction of ZIIHERA occurred in 10% of patients, and permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA occurred in 3.9% of patients.

In cycle 1, diarrhea at Grade 4 severity occurred in 1.5% and Grade 3 severity occurred in 15% of patients despite use of loperamide prophylaxis. The median time to onset for cycle 1 diarrhea was 6 days and median time to resolution was 18 days.

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy

Diarrhea was reported in 81% of 395 patients in clinical studies, including Grade 4 (1.3%), Grade 3 (20%) and Grade 2 (33%). Diarrhea leading to dose reduction of ZIIHERA occurred in 10% of patients, and permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA occurred in 1.8% of patients.

In cycle 1, diarrhea at Grade 4 severity occurred in 0.8% and Grade 3 severity occurred in 14% of patients despite use of loperamide prophylaxis. The median time to onset for cycle 1 diarrhea was 6 days and median time to resolution was 18 days.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity: Based on the mechanism of action, ZIIHERA can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. There are no human or animal data on the use of ZIIHERA in pregnancy. In literature reports, use of a HER2-directed antibody during pregnancy resulted in cases of oligohydramnios and oligohydramnios sequence manifesting as pulmonary hypoplasia, skeletal abnormalities, and neonatal death.

Verify the pregnancy status of females of reproductive potential prior to the initiation of ZIIHERA. Advise pregnant women and females of reproductive potential that exposure to ZIIHERA during pregnancy or within 4 months prior to conception can result in fetal harm. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception while receiving ZIIHERA and for 4 months following the last dose of ZIIHERA.

Left Ventricular Dysfunction (LVD): ZIIHERA can cause decreases in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).

Assess LVEF prior to initiation of ZIIHERA and at regular intervals during treatment. Withhold dose or permanently discontinue ZIIHERA based on severity of adverse reactions.

The safety of ZIIHERA has not been established in patients with a baseline ejection fraction that is < 50%.

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy and tislelizumab-jsgr

LVEF decrease (an absolute decline in LVEF of > 10%, resulting in a final value of < 50%) was observed in 9% of 330 patients in clinical studies. LVD leading to permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA was reported in 3% of patients. Fatal outcomes due to LVD occurred in one patient (0.3%). The median time to first occurrence of LVD was 6.9 months (range: 1.2 to 29.1 months). LVD resolved in 78% of patients.

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy

LVEF decrease was observed in 5% of 395 patients. LVD leading to permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA was reported in 1.0% of patients. The median time to first occurrence of LVD was 6.0 months (range: 1.4 to 15.0 months). LVD dysfunction resolved in 70% of patients. Infusion-Related Reactions: ZIIHERA can cause infusion-related reactions (IRRs).

Prior to each dose of ZIIHERA, administer premedication to prevent potential IRRs. Monitor patients for signs and symptoms of IRR during ZIIHERA administration and as clinically indicated after completion of infusion. Have medications and emergency equipment to treat IRRs available for immediate use.

If an IRR occurs, slow or stop the infusion, and administer appropriate medical management. Monitor patients until complete resolution of signs and symptoms before resuming. Permanently discontinue ZIIHERA in patients with recurrent severe or life-threatening IRRs.

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy and tislelizumab-jsgr

An IRR was reported in 22% of 330 patients in clinical studies, including Grade 4 (0.3%), Grade 3 (1.2%), and Grade 2 (16%) despite use of prophylaxis. IRRs leading to permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA were reported in 0.3% of patients. IRRs occurred on the first day of dosing in 17% of patients. Of all patients who experienced IRRs, 60% of reactions resolved within the first day.

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy

An IRR was reported in 24% of 395 patients in clinical studies, including Grade 4 (0.3%), Grade 3 (1.5%), and Grade 2 (18%) despite use of prophylaxis. IRRs leading to permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA were reported in 1.3% of patients. IRRs occurred on the first day of dosing in 22% of patients. Of all patients who experienced IRRs, 83% of reactions resolved within the first day.

Adverse Reactions

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy and tislelizumab-jsgr

Serious adverse reactions occurred in 59% of 294 patients in HERIZON-GEA-01. Serious adverse reactions in > 2% of patients included diarrhea (17%), IRR (5%), vomiting (4.8%), hypokalemia (4.4%), acute kidney injury (3.7%), pneumonia (3.7%), nausea (2.4%), decreased appetite (2.4%), and anemia (2.4%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 2.4% of patients and included acute kidney injury (N=2), cardiac failure, diarrhea, dehydration, hypovolemic shock and intestinal obstruction (all N=1).

Permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA occurred in 13% of patients. Adverse reactions that resulted in permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA in ≥ 1% of patients included diarrhea (4.4%) and ejection fraction decreased (2.7%).

The most common adverse reactions (≥ 20%) were diarrhea (83%), nausea (56%), decreased appetite (46%), vomiting (44%), hypokalemia (39%), fatigue (37%), rash (36%), peripheral neuropathy (27%), and IRR (25%).

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy

Serious adverse reactions occurred in 49% of 305 patients in HERIZON-GEA-01. Serious adverse reactions in > 2% of patients included diarrhea (11%), vomiting (3.3%), decreased appetite (2.6%), pneumonia (2.6%), sepsis (2.6%), hypokalemia (2.3%), and nausea (2.3%).

Permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA occurred in 10% of patients. Adverse reactions that resulted in permanent discontinuation of ZIIHERA in ≥ 1% of patients included ejection fraction decreased (2.0%), IRR (1.6%), and diarrhea (1.6%).

The most common adverse reactions (≥ 20%) were diarrhea (79%), nausea (54%), vomiting (44%), decreased appetite (40%), fatigue (36%), hypokalemia (33%), peripheral neuropathy (32%), IRR (25%), and rash (22%).

Pediatric Use: Safety and efficacy of ZIIHERA have not been established in pediatric patients.

Geriatric Use

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy and tislelizumab-jsgr

Of 302 patients randomized to ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy and tislelizumab-jsgr in HERIZON-GEA-01, there were 139 (46%) patients aged ≥ 65 years. One hundred and six (35%) were aged 65-74 years and 33 (11%) were aged ≥ 75 years.

There was a higher incidence of Grade ≥ 3 adverse reactions observed in patients aged ≥ 65 years (87%) as compared to younger patients (80%). The incidence of Grade 3 or 4 diarrhea was higher in patients aged ≥ 65 years (32%) compared to younger patients (20%).

There was an increased incidence of fatal adverse reactions in patients aged ≥ 65 years (4.4%); including acute kidney injury (N=2), cardiac failure, dehydration, hypovolemic shock and intestinal obstruction (all N=1), compared to younger patients (0.6%), including diarrhea (N=1).

ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy

Of 304 patients randomized to ZIIHERA in combination with chemotherapy in HERIZON-GEA-01, there were 130 (43%) patients aged ≥ 65 years. One hundred (33%) were aged 65-74 years and 30 (10%) were aged ≥ 75 years.

No overall differences in safety were observed between patients aged ≥ 65 years and younger adult patients.
